summary: In Greek mythology, Amatheia (Ancient Greek Ἀμάθεια, "she who rears/nurses" or "sparkling water") is the "fair-tressed" Nereid described with azure or luxuriant locks. One of the fifty sea-nymphs, she is a daughter of Nereus and the Oceanid Doris; Homer names her among Thetis' mourning sisters. Name variants include Æmathia, Amathea, and Amathia.
etymology: Ancient Greek Ἀμάθεια — interpreted as "rears, nurses" or "sparkling water"; a variant Amathia is glossed "queen of voice."

sections.heading: Fair-tressed Nereid
paragraphs: Amatheia appears in the Homeric catalogue of Nereids who surround Thetis in grief for Achilles. She has no independent myth beyond that catalogue role — a thin but named sea-sister in the atlas Nereid inventory.
Keep her distinct from other Amath- stems and from mortal eponyms that share similar spellings.
